speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to help me narrow down the cause, could you describe exactly when the swelling started and what activities seem to trigger it?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; at 18 months old, a swelling episode triggered by play without trauma, combined with a family history, strongly suggests a metabolic bone disorder. Have you noticed any recent changes in his appetite, or any unusual warmth or redness over the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pseudogout (Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Disease) in an infant is highly unlikely; given the age (18 months), trauma-free onset, and strong family history, the most probable diagnosis is a hereditary metabolic bone disorder such as Infantile Hypophosphatasia or a rare genetic arthropathy, though transient synovitis is less likely without fever. I will now request specific imaging to confirm the etiology. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_knee_Xray, Right_knee_Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Alkaline_Phosphatase, Serum_Calcium, Serum_Phosphate, Serum_Magnesium.
